key_insight: A finite-volume convolution unit (FVCU) extends CNN-based turbulence super-resolution from regular grids to arbitrary non-uniform and non-orthogonal meshes.
engineering_relevance: This enables fine-scale flow reconstruction on the kinds of meshes actually used in wall-bounded and complex-geometry CFD, without requiring remeshing to a structured grid.
method: Reformulate 3D convolution as successive axis-wise finite-volume operators.
Use gradient, averaging, and identity operators that work on general polyhedral cells.
Add Van Driest damping as a conditional wall-proximity input for physically informed reconstruction.
evidence_signal: The model was trained and tested on 4× coarsened turbulent channel-flow and circular-pipe-flow datasets, and also evaluated on an unseen elliptic pipe, recovering velocity fields, Reynolds stresses, anisotropy, and spectra beyond the coarse-grid Nyquist limit.
watch_item: Performance on unseen geometries shows slight overprediction of small-scale energy, so generalization and spectral fidelity should be checked carefully when deploying on new meshes.
paper_title: Extending convolutional neural networks to finite-volume meshes for fine-scale reconstruction of wall-bounded turbulence
